finding: @red-cup-engineering/web-server-services-section@0.1.0's startWebServer() reports a bound port but nothing accepts connections on it, so the ruled SERVER engine cannot serve on the Node transport today
reproduction: createWebApplicationEngine({ resources: [{ match: "/p", methods: ["GET"], handler: () => Response.json({ ok: true }) }] }) started with startWebServer(engine, 0) and again with startWebServer(engine, { port: 0, host: "127.0.0.1" }). Both resolve { server, port, address, close } with a plausible ephemeral port; fetch() to that port fails ECONNREFUSED in both call forms. The reproduction uses no x402-offer-seller-service code.
consequence: x402-offer-seller-service's ./node subpath, a two-line delegation to startWebServer, cannot be verified. Its Fetch face -- the face all five Cloudflare Workers sellers actually run on -- is unaffected and green.
relation: This is the ruled replacement for @red-cup-engineering/http-server-core-service, which web-source-evidence.mjs lists on LEGACY_SERVERS and whose own Node transport drops body-read refusals (recorded 2026-09-08 in paid-pacing-intelligence-gateway/data/records). Both Node transports are defective in different ways; the Fetch faces of both are sound. The supersession is therefore only half available today.
notDoneHere: Repair belongs to web-server-services-section's own custody, with its own consumers to re-pin. No workaround was added to the seller engine, and the two failing Node tests were left failing rather than deleted, because they encode the requirement the founder set.
